goal: Real liquid silhouettes on any mesh, not only shading ripples.
alternatives: Normal-only wobble (the core's Wobble: silhouette unchanged); a GLSL TOP or SDF raymarcher (only shapes written as distance functions); vertex displacement in the GLSL MAT; CPU/SOP noise (Noise SOP) feeding the material.

choice: Vertex displacement inside the same GLSL MAT that draws the glass, computed in object space before TDDeform.
consequence: Any Geometry COMP can use the material with no extra SOPs. The silhouette changes (test silhouette_coverage_changes). The mesh must have enough vertices for the field (documented; coarse_mesh experiment). SOP-side tools such as collisions or physics do not see the motion.

goal: Keep the core look exactly, so the 12 presets and every core control keep working.
alternatives: Rewrite the pixel shader; include the core shader through TouchDesigner's #include; copy it verbatim with additions.

Zeros for extra colour buffers, which this study added first, are now part of the core. A unit test compares every added and removed line with that list; a preview test asserts Amplitude 0 renders bit-identically to the current core (checks/core_reference) for all 12 presets, and another renders the moving glass through the flow and the core pixel shaders and finds no difference.
consequence: Fixes to the core pixel shader must be copied here by hand and checks/core_reference refreshed; the diff test and the two preview tests show any divergence. Rebased on the core working tree after family-sync merge, on 6a58487 (family sync).

goal: Normals that follow any field the user writes.
alternatives: Analytic derivatives of each ingredient (fast, but every new ingredient needs its own derivative); a Jacobian formula for one specific map (resonant-foil, exact but not general); finite differences of the moved surface (Fugaro's neighbour method in the archive).
evidence: caustics-in-webgl.mdx 700-816 and field-guide-to-tsl-and-webgpu.mdx 360-434 use the neighbour method on arbitrary noise.
choice: Neighbour method with central differences along two tangents (four extra field evaluations), offsets taken relative to the point, nudge 1e-3 object sizes, sign kept outside. The result is cross(J t1, J t2), the cofactor-transformed normal.
consequence: Any new field term gets correct normals for free. Costs five field evaluations per vertex (vertex stage only). In crack-free mode the normals are within 0.5 degrees of float64 finite-difference normals of the moved surface in nine cases, including non-uniform scale and a week of flow (test normals_match_finite_differences, max 0.17 degrees), and within 1 degree at the Amplitude maximum where the field squeezes the surface (0.82). The rest normal is kept only at a fold (decision on the fallback below). Normal mode reuses the point's normal and is approximate (up to 10 degrees on the demo torus at preset amplitudes, 64 at Amplitude 0.5).

goal: No cracks on meshes whose vertices share positions but not normals (hard edges, some UV seams).
alternatives: Always displace along the normal (classic blob; cracks); ask the user to consolidate points (Facet SOP) first; displace along a direction that depends on position only.
evidence: Derivative's Box SOP page: by default 6 separate faces, 4 points per corner. The TSL guide's position-only displacement (pos + noise) cannot crack.
choice: Displace along: menu with 'Away from centre (crack-free)', the default, and 'Normal'. The centre direction is normalize(position - Flow centre). The field reads position only, never UV. Geometry without normals always uses the centre direction. Within 0.05 object sizes of the centre the direction fades smoothly to zero (smoothstep), so a point at the centre stays put instead of jumping along its own normal (independent review M8).
consequence: Crack-free is guaranteed (test crack_free_keeps_coincident_vertices_together: gap under 1e-5, zero holes). Trade-off: where the surface does not face away from the centre (the top of a torus tube, a flat sheet through the centre) part of the motion slides sideways and shows less; use Normal mode for open sheets and smooth meshes far from star-shaped.

goal: Presets that transfer across object sizes and positions.
alternatives: Amplitude and scales in raw SOP units; Flow centre and Object size typed by hand; the same, filled in from the SOP's bounds by the component's Python.
evidence: A GLSL MAT does not know its geometry's bounds, but the component's Python does: SOP.bounds() returns centre and size in SOP space (docs.derivative.ca/SOP_Class). One material can be shared by several objects (independent review T4).
choice: Flow centre and Object size (about the object's radius) on the Flow fit page, plus a 'Fit to Glass geometry' pulse that sets them from the rendered SOP of Inputs > Glass geometry (native.fit_flow). The field works in q = (P - centre) / size; Amplitude is a fraction of that size and scales are features per object size.
consequence: A preset looks alike on a 1-unit sphere and a 10-unit model away from the origin (test motion_matches_float64_reference, case model_x10_off_origin). One press fits a new object; one component fits one object size. Not run at build time: the defaults already fit the demo sphere. Fit pulse pending a native check. Family sync C8: the same Object size now also scales Thickness and Frost and divides Tint density, Wobble scale and the film swirl, so the glass look carries over too (test object_size_carries_presets_over).
status: superseded by Family close G1: Flow size, not Object size, is now the motion's unit (q = (P - centre) / Flow size), and Object size sizes the glass only; the goal stands. Native Fit pending (validation.json fit_native)

goal: A gravity sag and drips that point down in the world.
alternatives: Sag along the object's own -Y (rotates with the object); world gravity brought into object space.
evidence: Reference 3 shows a blob with hanging droplets; the demo object spins.
choice: Gravity direction in world space, converted with mat3(uTDMats[].worldInverse) and then the inverse of TDInstanceMat3() (skipped when that matrix is singular); Sag pulls the part below the centre along it, Drip gathers it into lumps chosen by a noise across the fall direction.
consequence: World-down through object rotation, non-uniform scale and each instance's rotation and scale (test gravity_stays_world_down, max 0.008 degrees in the preview). TDInstanceMat3() with instancing off is assumed to be identity; pending a native check. Sag is a position-only offset, so it never cracks.

goal: Instances that do not all ripple in step.
alternatives: Identical motion for every instance; per-instance phase from TDInstanceID().
evidence: Derivative documents int TDInstanceID() in the vertex stage.
choice: Instance variation offsets where each instance reads the field: seed = variation * 100 * fract(id * R3 constants).
consequence: Variation 0 keeps instances identical (test instance_variation). Instance transforms still apply through TDDeform after the motion.

goal: Exact still glass at Amplitude 0.
alternatives: Let the maths reduce to zero (normalisation drift, extra cost); an explicit branch.
evidence: resonant-foil found a tiny difference from renormalising an already normal vector.
choice: if (uFlow.x != 0.0) guards all flow work; otherwise the vertex stage does exactly what the core's does.
consequence: Bit-identical to the core in the preview (amplitude0_matches_core, amplitude0_vertex_identity). Morphing Amplitude through 0 has no visible jump because the moved surface converges to the rest surface.

goal: Teach the motion separately from the look.
alternatives: Only the final image; a separate debug material.
evidence: The archived Blob colours the sphere by its displacement varying.
choice: A 'Displacement' teaching stage (orange out, blue in) fed by vFlow, plus a Correct normals toggle for the wrong-normals comparison and demo shapes (sphere, torus, box, grid) with a detail control.
consequence: Each experiment changes one thing on the same component.

goal: Flow speed and Morph can be animated without the liquid jumping (independent review T1, M2).
alternatives: Time = absTime x speed (jumps by absTime x change of speed); a Speed CHOP integrating the morphed speed (CHOP samples are 32-bit, so a slow speed stalls once the sum is large); an Execute DAT accumulating each frame into a parameter; a clock in the presets module, advanced by the uniform expression itself.
evidence: A 2 s Morph from Prism Chrome to Amber Honey one hour after start moved the surface 438x faster than a still frame, backwards (reviewer harness rerun before the fix). absTime.seconds is a Python float (docs.derivative.ca/AbsTime_Class); uniform expressions that reference absTime re-evaluate every frame, as the core's absTime binding already relies on.
choice: presets.clock(speed_par, absTime.seconds, wrap): adds u(speed) x elapsed seconds in Python floats, returns the same value for the same frame (both materials), gives Fixed time x speed with Pause on, and wraps flow time at 25600 s. uFlow.w and uWobble.w are clocks (uFlow.y unused, uWobble.z = 1); Demo spin uses one too.
consequence: A speed change changes only how fast the liquid moves: per-frame travel during that Morph stays within 2x of the 2-second value after an hour and a day (test flow_time_follows_speed; unit test of the clock). The clock restarts (one jump) when the presets module reloads. Native evaluation order pending. Family sync R1: clock() was replaced by the core's advance(), which keeps per-component state and never needs absTime in an expression (see 'Family sync R1').
status: superseded in part by the family sync (R1): same integration, shared advance()

goal: Rebuilt normals that stay precise however long TouchDesigner runs (independent review T2, M1).
alternatives: Leave time unbounded (normals off by 10 degrees after a day in float32); a larger nudge (about 10x less error, more truncation); split the drift into whole cells and a fraction; also wrap time on the CPU.
evidence: Rerun of the reviewer's harness before the fix: default look, normals vs float64 max 0.62 degrees at 1 h, 10.1 degrees at 24 h.
choice: The noise lattice repeats every 256 cells: the hash reads ((c + 128) & 255) - 128, which leaves cells -128 to 127 unchanged, so the look is the same. driftNoise() folds each drift into one repeat, adds the whole cells to the lattice index and only the fraction to the position. Flow time wraps at 25600 s, where every drift rate (a multiple of 0.01 cells per second) has moved whole repeats. The wave's phase goes through fract().
consequence: After 24 h the normals are within 0.10 degrees of float64, after a week at speed 0.9 within 0.08; positions within 0.0001 object sizes (tests normals_match_finite_differences, motion_matches_float64_reference). Wobble and film time were unwrapped until the family sync, which brought the core's uPhase drift wrapped at 256 (test ripples_and_film_exact_after_a_week).

goal: A demo box that renders in TouchDesigner and still has split normals along its edges (independent review T3).
alternatives: Box SOP with Use Divisions (renders nothing: 'the Divisions consist of open polygons'); Box SOP plus Divide SOP (point sharing unverified); one Grid SOP turned onto six faces with Transform SOPs and merged.
evidence: docs.derivative.ca/Box_SOP, parameter dodivs. The preview already built its box from six separate grids.
choice: demo_geo/box_face (Grid SOP, 1.5 x 1.5, rows and cols from Demo detail) -> six Transform SOPs -> demo_geo/box (Merge SOP) -> Switch input 2.
consequence: The cracks and crack_free experiments should render natively; the preview geometry now matches the recipe. Parameter names follow Derivative's pages; the native build is still to be checked (demo nodes are lenient).

goal: Behave in users' scenes with Render Pick and multi-buffer Render TOPs (independent review T6).
alternatives: Leave as in the core (pick values and extra buffers undefined); follow Derivative's documented patterns.
evidence: Write a GLSL MAT, sections Picking and Multiple Render Targets.
choice: Vertex: under #ifdef TD_PICKING_ACTIVE, TDWritePickingValues() then the moved positions and normals into vTDPickVert. Pixel: fragColor[TD_NUM_COLOR_BUFFERS]; buffers 1-7 get zeros under #if, with constant indices (WebGL and some backends reject a loop index).
consequence: Compiles with glslang in both variants and in WebGL2; native picking and multi-buffer renders are untested. Buffers beyond 8 stay undefined. Family sync C2: the core adopted this pattern; the pixel stage now also has an #ifndef fallback of one buffer, and the compile check covers 3 and 8 buffers and the fallback. Family close G6: the vertex shader now uses the form Derivative's Write a GLSL MAT page prints, '#ifndef TD_PICKING_ACTIVE ... #else TDWritePickingValues(); #endif' (the page: when picking, only the #else block runs). The point is moved and placed before the branch; the #else block writes the pick values, then the moved positions and normals (see the family close G6 entry).

goal: Family sync R1: one integrator for every moving value, the better of this study's clock() and the core's advance().
alternatives: Keep clock(speed_par, absTime.seconds, wrap); adopt advance() everywhere; per-rate phases for the vertex field too (eight more values in uniforms).
evidence: Both add speed x frame time in Python doubles, give Fixed time x speed while paused and the same value within a frame. clock() kept its running value per parameter name, so two flow components in one project shared one value (unit test test_two_components_keep_their_own_motion fails on 6a58487 code); its expressions read absTime, so a still look recooked every frame; its wobble time was unwrapped (float32 rounding in the pixel noise). advance() keys by component path, reads absTime only when moving, and the core wraps the ripple and film drift to 256. This study's folded drift (one flow time wrapped at 25600, folded into the 256-cell lattice in the shader) keeps the vertex field within 0.10 degrees of float64 after a day and 0.08 after a week with one uniform value.
choice: advance() is the only integrator: flow_time() = advance(comp, 'flow', u(Flowspeed), 25600) feeds uFlow.w; phase() feeds the core's uPhase; spin() turns the demo. The vertex shader keeps its folded drift (better here than eight per-rate phases). clock() is removed.
consequence: No node expression reads absTime; two components move independently; speed 0 holds and stops the per-frame updates. Tests: unit tests for a 100-frame morph and a slider drag at 1 h (flow time and the four phases), within-frame agreement, pause and resume, two components, a still look; preview tests morph_frame_is_smooth_after_an_hour, speed_change_is_smooth_after_an_hour, ripples_and_film_exact_after_a_week, flow_time_follows_speed and the week-long normals test.

goal: Family sync R2: glass that sits inside the user's scene, with objects in front of it still in front.
alternatives: Glass-only render plus Over TOP (6a58487 README step 5); the core's Render Pass TOP on the scene render.
evidence: Core audit round 2 (C1, D5): with a Refraction TOP the glass writes alpha 1, so an Over TOP paints it over foreground objects. Render Pass TOP page (read 2026-11-02): Clear Depth Buffer (cleardepth), Clear to Camera Color (cleartocamcolor), Override Material (overridemat).
choice: README and tutorial draw the glass with a Render Pass TOP after the scene render (Clear Depth Buffer and Clear to Camera Color off, Override Material = material). The demo render overrides its material the same way, and demo_geo no longer references the material. The Over TOP stays as the documented fallback and in the demo, whose backdrop is a flat GLSL TOP.
consequence: Occlusion comes from the scene's own depth buffer. Whether a material may sample the render its pass builds on is unverified natively for every member; the fallback loses occlusion. Verifier gap round G2: the preview now tests the claim (render_pass_keeps_foreground_in_front, ported from Liquid Glass Prism): an opaque ball in front of the moving glass stays exactly as in the scene render with the Render Pass route (max 1/255), while the Over TOP control paints the glass over it (max 246/255).

goal: Family sync R5 to R9 and C1, C2, C4 to C7: the core's hardening and the family's merge items in this study's pixel stage and recipe.
alternatives: Adopt each item; skip items that do not apply.
evidence: Every item applies: this study uses the core pixel stage, a back-face pass, the built-in studio, frost, colours and the same recipe. Items already here: picking with the moved surface and extra colour buffers (C2, this study's own fix T6), the 256-cell vertex lattice (R1).
choice: Taken with the core pixel shader: derivatives at the top of main(), relative degeneracy threshold, faceCamera() after wobble, wobble scaled by the cube root of |det(world)|, azimuth(), guarded light and half vectors, per-sample IOR >= 1, r0 * r0, ordered smoothstep edges (also env.frag and backdrop.frag), R2 frost disc, flat-image blur widened by the warp, rgba32float back-face pass read with a masked texelFetch bilinear at nearest filter, orthographic distances, Colour parameters and Energy conserving, the scene alpha (covered), the colour cap, measured screen orientation, fog. Vertex shader: a zero normal is decided before TDDeformNorm, and the rebuilt normal is safely normalised. Recipe: extend modes, presets.menu(), Dither off (lenient, 'dither' warning), Info DATs on every render, script_errors, blocking_errors and render_diagnostics in inspect().
consequence: Each item has a test (review.md, Family sync). Over the opaque demo scene the moving presets render like the core's 6a58487 pixel stage within 1/255, except one Liquid Mercury silhouette pixel on the screen's centre column (next entry).

goal: Family sync C6 finding: the measured screen orientation can flip one silhouette pixel on the screen's centre lines.
alternatives: Keep the core's screenSign() unchanged; add a dead zone of two pixels around the centre lines here only; report it to the core.
evidence: opaque_scene_matches_pre_sync: Liquid Mercury, pixel (240, 214) at 480 x 270, the centre column on the bottom silhouette, differs from the core's 6a58487 pixel stage by 8/255 in the final image and 49/255 in the refraction stage. A scratch copy whose screenSign() only flips when the pixel is more than two pixels from the centre line gave 0 differing pixels on four presets. Cause: with multisampling the pixel is shaded at its centre, outside its silhouette triangle, so the interpolated point projects up to a pixel away, and on the centre column that can cross 0.
choice: Keep the core's code (this pixel stage must equal the core's, max difference 0); report the finding to the core as an open item; the preview test counts the centre lines apart (at most 2 pixels over 1/255).
consequence: At most one or two silhouette pixels per frame on the centre lines can bend the wrong way horizontally; invisible in the captures. A dead-zone fix belongs in the core. Family close G2: the core adopted Liquid Glass Lit's tie-break (on a centre line the projected position's screen derivative decides, where 1/w changes by under 10% to the next pixel), and this pixel stage follows it. The new preview test screen_orientation_has_no_wrong_pixels measures the moving glass: at most 1 wrong single-sample pixel and 5 wrong multisampled pixels per row of twelve renders (c94e849: 1,932 to 2,016 on the centre row of the odd size in a flipped raster). The multisampled silhouette pixels this finding describes remain, a few per row (thresholds as in Lit and the core: 2 and 20; 2 and 10 since the family critic's centre-line residual round, last entry).
status: closed by the core's family close G2; preview test passes here

goal: Family sync C3 (conditional): continuous dispersion without dithering through the fan-gap mip level from Liquid Glass Blobs.
alternatives: Keep mip 0 for dispersion (current core); the whole fan gap; a quarter of it (what Blobs adopted); Prism's isotropic footprintLod (not tried: core round-2 B7 measured it worse).
evidence: Round-2 B7 method in the preview, 480 x 270, Dispersion 1, Samples 12, against the current shader at 64 samples, Clear Crystal and Prism Chrome on the moving sphere and the torus, refraction and final stages, preset Thickness and 2.5 (checks/results/c3-fan-gap.json). Whole gap, mean error on the changed pixels: 1.05 vs 0.70 (Clear Crystal sphere refraction), 5.91 vs 2.18 at Thickness 2.5, 5.09 vs 1.68 (Prism Chrome sphere refraction, 2.5), 4.06 vs 1.42 (Clear Crystal torus, 2.5); glass pixels over 32/255: up to 59 vs 0. Worse in all 16 cases. A quarter of the gap changed no pixel at this resolution (the gap stays below one texel).
choice: Rejected, as in the core. New preview test dispersion_converges_with_samples pins the agreement on the moving sphere (12 vs 64 samples: mean within 1/255, within 2.5/255 at Thickness 2.5, no pixel over 32/255; measured 0.46, 0.54, 2.02 and 1.57).
consequence: Rainbow fringes stay sharp; very thick glass on sharp scenes can still show steps at 12 samples (raise Samples).

goal: Family sync C8: presets carry over between a 0.1-unit and a 10-unit object, with one Object size.
alternatives: The core's Object size (scene units, relative to the demo torus, multiplied by the Geometry COMP's world scale) next to this study's Flowsize (SOP units); one control in SOP units for both.
evidence: The motion must be in SOP units (it happens before TDDeform). Two size controls with the same label would break one name per thing; the identity at size 1 forces one space to ignore a Geometry COMP's scale (the core made the same trade, the other way round).
choice: One control: Flow fit > Object size (internal name Objectsize, renamed from Flowsize; setup, default 1, min 0.001). It scales the motion as before and, like the core's, multiplies Thickness and Frost and divides Tint density, Wobble scale and the film swirl frequency. Fit to Glass geometry (native.fit_flow) sets it and Flow centre from the rendered SOP's bounds and reports a scaled Geometry COMP. The film swirl frequency is uFilm.w = 2.5 / Object size; set by hand to 0, it gives one film thickness over the whole object, no swirl, which still drifts with uPhase.w until Wobble speed is 0 (verifier gap round G1; the README first said '0 freezes the swirl').
consequence: Object size 1 gives the 6a58487 uniform values exactly (unit test). A 0.1-unit and a 10-unit sphere render like the 1-unit one within 2/255 (object_size_carries_presets_over). On a scaled Geometry COMP the glass lengths stay at the unscaled size (documented; scale the SOP instead). Verifier round V2: this Object size is not Liquid Glass's. Liquid Glass's Fit sets radius x world scale / 1.45 (1 = its demo torus); this one is half the SOP's largest side (1 = the demo sphere). On the same unscaled object this value, and with it every glass length, is 1.45 times Liquid Glass's after each Fit (demo torus, Amplitude 0: up to 240/255 apart; with the same value in both: 0). Documented in the README and tutorial; fit_flow() reports liquid_glass_object_size = size x world scale / 1.45. A core-equivalent Object size here was rejected: it would change every preset's look at the default Object size and split the one size control into two meanings.
status: superseded in part by the family close G1 (Flow size and Object size; see that entry); native Fit pending

evidence: Render TOP and Render Pass TOP pages (Render Pass TOP read 2026-11-02): parameter dither, default not stated. Write a GLSL MAT (last edited 2026-08-05): TDDither() applies only when called. Prism's backdrop.frag at 6a58487, through the core's port with ordered smoothstep edges.

Study > Backdrop (Checker default, Type) drives uBackdrop through presets.menu(); presets-sheet.png and presets-sheet-type.png show the twelve presets on both.

goal: Verifier round V1: rebuilt normals that stay right wherever the surface is squeezed, with a safe answer where it folds.
alternatives: normalize() with no fallback (6a58487: NaN possible at an exact zero); an absolute 1e-12 threshold on the cross product's squared length (family sync: also caught squeezed, unfolded surfaces, because the unmoved value is only (2e)^4 = 1.6e-11); a threshold relative to the nudge's rest area; a fallback only for exact zero or NaN.
evidence: Float64 scan and GPU check, Chrome Type motion at Amplitude 0.5 on the demo sphere, flow time 2: 196 vertices squeezed to under a quarter of their rest area (smallest 0.16), none folded; the absolute threshold put 194 normals more than 5 degrees off (max 46.3); normalize() gave max 0.82. Estimate, not measured: float32 rounding in the moved steps is about 1e-7 object sizes against a step of 2e = 2e-3, so the cross product's direction is reliable to a few degrees down to about a thousandth of the rest area.
choice: flowNormal() returns the unit normal and keeps the rest normal only when dot(m, m) <= 1e-6 x (2e)^4 (under a thousandth of the rest area) or m is NaN. The vertex shader's safeNormalize() helper went away (it had no other caller).
consequence: Squeezed points keep their rebuilt normals (test case squeezed_chrome_type_amplitude_0_5: max 0.82 degrees, tolerance 1). Only points at a fold line take the rest normal. No preview changed (56 captures bit-identical): no preset or experiment is squeezed under a quarter of its area.
status: implemented; preview and unit tests pass; native pending

goal: Family close G1: Object size has one meaning across the family, while the motion keeps a size in the SOP's units.

(c) Two controls, one job each: Flow size for the motion (SOP units, the name and binding of 6a58487's Flowsize, uFlowSpace.w only) and Object size with the family meaning for the glass; Fit to Glass geometry sets both from the same object. For (c), the default Object size: (c1) 1, the core's default (the demo look stays as it was, but Fit on the demo sphere then sets 0.69 and the look jumps), or (c2) 1 / 1.45 = 0.69, what Fit sets on the default demo object (the defaults keep fitting the demo, as decision 'Presets that transfer' states, and the demo shows the presets at the relative thickness they were tuned at on the core's torus).
evidence: Family rule: Liquid Glass Lit decisions.json, family_rule (reference radius 1.45; lengths x Object size; ripple and film lookups x worldScale()). On the core demo torus scaled 3 by its COMP the critic measured Fit 1.45 here; now 3.0, equal to the core's own fit_glass() on the same geometry (unit test_g1_object_size_follows_the_family_rule; c94e849: 1.45). Preview fit_size_carries_presets_over_comp_scale (Lit's cases with the motion on, COMP scale 0.1 and 10, Object size = scale x default, Flow size unchanged): every case max 1/255, 0 pixels over 8. On c94e849 with its own Fit values (Object size unchanged on a COMP-scaled object) the ripple and film stages matched (1/255), but the final images differed by 30 to 247/255 on 9,609 to 20,679 pixels over 8/255: the glass lengths missed the COMP's scale. The same test with Object size = k on c94e849 also scales its motion (one size for both): 245 to 255/255.
choice: (c) with (c2). New control Flow fit > Flow size (Flowsize; setup, default 1, min 0.001, max 100) bound to uFlowSpace.w only; Object size (Objectsize; setup, default 1 / 1.45) bound only to the glass lengths, as in the core. fit_flow() sets Flow centre and Flow size from the rendered SOP's bounds and Object size = half the largest side x the COMP's world scale / 1.45; its report drops liquid_glass_object_size (the two are now the same). The Flow page labels say 'flow size'; the Fit label says it sets Flow centre, Flow size and Object size. The pixel stage's worldScale() lookups come with the re-sync.
consequence: On the same object, Object size now equals the core's and Lit's, so a preset looks the same in all three at Amplitude 0. The default demo look changes once: the glass on the radius-1 demo sphere is sized for Object size 0.69 instead of 1, so it is thinner relative to the sphere and its ripples and film bands are 1.45 times finer, as the presets look on the core's torus (review.md, Family close, visible changes, with numbers). Existing objects: a component built before this change keeps its old Object size value; its motion is unaffected only once Flow size is set (a rebuilt component starts at the defaults; press Fit). Objects of very different sizes still need their own component. Fit reads the first object for both sizes (the family rule's 'several objects: the largest' does not apply, because the motion has one centre). Non-uniform scale counts as its average; per-instance scale is not seen by Object size.

goal: Family critic: one Object size per component. One Fit press sets one Object size for the whole component; say what that does on several objects of different sizes, on a Geometry COMP scale that changes after Fit and on per-instance scale, and decide whether to change the family rule.
alternatives: (a) Keep the family rule (Object size = world radius / 1.45, set by Fit) and document the three setups as measured, with workarounds: one copy of the component per size; press Fit again after a scale change, or animate Object size by the same factor. (b) The critic's proposal: Object size in SOP units, set by Fit; the shader multiplies the lengths and the pattern lookups by worldScale() and by a per-instance factor that the vertex stage computes (a flat varying, the cube root of |det(TDInstanceMat3())|), and turns the ripple slope by the instance rotation. COMP and instance scale, animation included, would then follow without Fit, and Flow size and Object size could become one value again. (c) Ask the user first.
evidence: Measured with this study's own Fit code, uniform expressions and shader lookups on fake TouchDesigner objects (checks/results/red-run-family-critic.json, measurement; ratio = value / what a Fit that sees the true world size gives): Fit at COMP scale 3: Object size 3.0, lengths and patterns 1. Two objects of radius 1.45 and 0.29: Fit reads only the first object: listed large first, the small one gets lengths and patterns 5 times its own; listed small first, the large one gets 0.2 times and Flow size 0.29. COMP Scale 1 to 3 after Fit: lengths 1/3, ripple and film periods 1/3; with Object size times 3: all 1. An instance scaled 3: lengths 1/3, ripple and film periods 1 (the lookups use the SOP position, which the instance scales; worldScale() reads uTDMats[vCamIndex].world, without the instance). The ripple slope is turned by worldForNormals only, so it ignores an instance's rotation. Two of the critic's descriptions differ from the measurement: with an animated COMP scale the patterns keep Fit's world size like the lengths (they do not follow live), and with per-instance scale the patterns do follow; only the lengths stay. Option (b) changes what a typed Object size means on a scaled COMP, touches every member's pixel and vertex stage, Flow's checks/core_reference and Lit's family_rule, needs a native check of TDInstanceMat3() in each vertex stage, and still leaves several objects of different SOP sizes on one Object size.
choice: (a) now, with (b) recorded for the user's decision (c). The critic marked (b) as needing the user's decision, and this round asks no questions (co-design.json).
consequence: README note 'One Object size per component' and one Limits point in the article, pinned to the measurement by test_one_object_size_setups_are_measured_and_documented. No shader, preset, uniform expression or capture changed; the look did not change. If the user picks (b), the whole family changes together and the family_rule record in Liquid Glass Lit's decisions.json is rewritten.
status: implemented as (a) (docs and tests); (b) pending the user's decision; not run in TouchDesigner

goal: Family critic (low): the COMP-scale test's threshold matches what the test measures.
alternatives: (a) Keep 'at most 50 pixels over 8/255' and only reword the docs. (b) Replace it with 'at most 2/255 at every pixel'. (c) Add 'at most 2/255 at every pixel' and keep the shared 50-pixel clause. (d) Hold 1/255, the measured value.
evidence: Every case measures 1/255 (6 cases at COMP scale 0.1 and 10). Liquid Glass Lit's family_rule record said the test holds 1/255 (Lit corrected it in this round). A scratch copy with the worldScale() exponent 0.3333 instead of 1.0 / 3.0 in liquid_flow.frag (world scale 9.9977 instead of 10) gives film stage 4/255, Oil Slick final 5/255, Aqua Jelly and Prism Chrome finals 2/255; 0 pixels over 8/255: before the fix the test passed when run alone (TESTS filter); with it the test fails when run alone (TESTS filter). Here amplitude0_matches_core already caught the same slip (up to 2/255 on 3 of its 23 renders, the torus scaled 3 by its COMP), so the gap was in the fit test's own claim. The suite's exact-match tests (ior1_is_invisible and others) use 2/255.
choice: (c). The pass condition is x.max <= 2 && x.pixelsOver8 <= 50 in the core, Flow and Lit. The shared clause keeps the test shape the same in all five members; Prism and Blobs keep their own bounds. 2/255 leaves one step of rounding above the measurement, as the exact-match tests do.
consequence: A pattern-scale slip as small as the exponent 0.3333 fails the test. The docs say what the test holds. A GPU that rounds differently could put a case at 3/255; read the evidence before loosening. The tests run in Chromium SwiftShader only; the native COMP-scale check is still pending.

goal: Family critic (low): the antialiased centre-line residual. With multisampling, a few silhouette pixels near a centre line still take the wrong orientation sign (up to 8 per row of twelve renders in the members' surveys). In Liquid Glass Lit's survey a centroid-sampled position, form (e), removed most of those in the usual raster, but it needs a centroid-qualified vertex output that no TouchDesigner build has run.
alternatives: (a) Adopt form (e) now in every member: a second vertex output with the centroid qualifier, read only for the projected position. (b) Adopt it now in one member. (c) Keep the current tie-break; make the residual one family open question with a native check that measures whether it is visible, and try (e) in Liquid Glass Lit first only if it is. (d) Leave the known-limit notes as they are.
evidence: Reproduced on this study (WebGL preview, Chromium SwiftShader; not TouchDesigner). screen_orientation_has_no_wrong_pixels: 11 wrong multisampled pixels in 144 renders, at most 5 per row of twelve (2 in the normal raster), and 1 wrong single-sample pixel. Final image (checks/results/centre-line-residual.json; each render drawn as delivered and with the orientation set to the right value, 4x multisampled canvas): 8 pixels change in 144 renders, at most 4 per row, 4 by more than 8/255, the largest by 38/255 (Violet Gel on the knot, normal raster, 480 x 270); in the normal raster, TouchDesigner's usual orientation, 2 pixels, by up to 38/255. All lie within 4 pixels of a centre line. Across the core, Flow, Lit and Prism the largest change is 43/255, at most 7 pixels per row. Looked at 8 times enlarged next to the right-sign render, the core's 43/255 pixel reads as one rim pixel a little darker than its neighbours. Lit's survey measured form (e) over 576 renders: the multisampled residual went from 17 to 1 pixel in the normal raster and from 18 to 16 in the flipped raster. A scratch copy of Lit with a centroid output compiles in glslang (58 of 58, GLSL 4.60 and Vulkan SPIR-V), which says nothing about a TouchDesigner build. Before this round the residual was a known limit here (decision 'Family sync C6 finding'), only Liquid Glass Lit listed it as an open question, in its own words, and no native check covered the residual.
choice: (c), the critic's fix. (a) and (b) would change shaders on a qualifier that no TouchDesigner build has run, for pixels that may not be visible; (d) gives no way to settle it. The open question has the same words in the core, Flow, Lit and Prism (co-design.json). validation.json family_close.native_run gains centre_line_residual: render the delivered material and a copy with the orientation set to the right value, take the difference (Composite TOP, Difference; Analyze TOP, Maximum in RGB) and look at those pixels at 100% zoom. The preview test now allows at most 10 wrong multisampled pixels per row (20 before; measured at most 5 here), so the range the question states stays guarded. This study's pixel stage must equal the core's (amplitude0_matches_core), so it takes form (e) only with the core's pixel stage.
consequence: No shader, preset, uniform expression or capture changes. The residual stays as measured until the native check answers. If it is visible, Liquid Glass Lit tries (e) first, with its survey and this check; then the core, with Flow, and Prism. If it is not, the question closes with the native record.
status: implemented as an open family question; native check centre_line_residual pending; unit tests CentreLineResidual (2) fail on the files before this round
